item.title: Workrave 1.11.2
item.description:
Workrave 1.11.2 has been released. You can now choose which speakers or headphones play your break reminders. This release also fixes several problems that could cause Workrave to crash or lose saved timer progress and statistics.
- New features and improvements: - You can now choose which speakers or headphones Workrave uses in the sound preferences on Windows, Linux, and macOS. For example, you can play break reminders through your speakers while other sounds use your headphones (#700, koloved) - Improved error reports to help us investigate problems - Bug fixes: - Fixed incorrect break timer settings when using Workrave for the first time - Workrave now uses the default timer settings if saved settings are missing or damaged - Fixed a problem that could prevent Workrave from starting on Windows if saved settings were damaged - Fixed problems starting Workrave when exercise files were missing or damaged - Fixed crashes when Workrave could not save timer progress or statistics, or delete statistics history, for example because another program was using the files - Workrave now keeps the previously saved timer progress and statistics if saving new data fails - Fixed a crash that could occur when a break reminder appeared on Windows - Restored missing icons in the tray and timer-window menus on Windows (#736)

commit 0f2c95feacf3f3080077f309b72687aa196ef2bb Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-11T14:42:53+02:00
fix(corenext): don't let a failed history delete terminate the process
Statistics::delete_all_history still used the throwing overloads of is_regular_file and remove. It runs from the statistics dialog's button handler -- a glibmm slot -- so on Windows a history file held open by something else would end the process the same way group 5747eb4f does, via glibmm's unhandled-exception g_error. libs/core got this in 5e4f876d5; corenext's copy was missed. Same change, same log line.
That was the last throwing filesystem call in either core. The rest of the tree's are startup-only or already inside a try.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit 64417eeb6ff087fed3ae34bd4d32f65d6ccb1a77 Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-11T14:35:41+02:00
fix(core): don't let a failed state write terminate the process
Core::save_state runs from the heartbeat once a minute, in the same tick as the statistics save, and ended with the throwing overload of std::filesystem::rename. On Windows the rename fails whenever something else holds the state file open at that instant -- a sync client on a redirected AppData\Roaming, a scanner -- and the exception unwinds out of the glibmm timeout slot, where glibmm turns it into g_error and aborts. Guardrail group 5747eb4f: four users in three days on 1.11.1, every crash at hh:mm:00.
5e4f876d5 already made the statistics save survive this; give the timer state the same treatment, since the two are indistinguishable in the stack.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

item.title: Workrave 1.11.1-30
item.description:
Workrave 1.11.1 has been released. This release fixes several Windows installation issues. This release contains no functional changes to Workrave itself; all changes are limited to the Windows installer.
- Bug fixes: - Fixed missing Microsoft Visual C++ runtime dependency on Windows, which could cause Workrave to fail to start with a "VCRUNTIME140.dll was not found" error - Fixed an issue where the installer would repeatedly claim Workrave was still running and refuse to continue, even when it wasn't - Fixed the installed version number not being shown for Workrave in the Windows "Apps & Features" list - Fixed an issue where the installer did not uninstall Workrave 1.10 when upgrading, leaving both versions installed side by side
commit 97f2ff74eb26532593c9228f2a61683d1f75c338 Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-07T19:54:44+02:00
fix: test unconvertible settings only on windows
commit 444b6499af1862aebb4e57c52cc351e591cdb355 Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-06T22:03:15+02:00
fix(gtkmm): don't take a window handle from an unrealized widget
Crash group a0ace781, 20 crashes since 30 July, is a read of 0xf8 inside libgdk from GtkUtil.cc:498 by way of BreakWindow.cc:730 -- the second set_always_on_top in BreakWindow::start, the one after show_all. The frame for start() is cfi, so the line is reliable.
GDK_WINDOW_HWND is gdk_win32_window_get_handle, which dereferences the GdkWindow without checking it. gtk_widget_get_window returns nullptr for an unrealized widget, and a null plus a struct field offset is exactly the address in the report. realize_if_needed at the top of start() covers the first call; by the second the widget is no longer realized.
What unrealizes it is still open. Everything between the two calls -- update_break_window, center, showing the desktop window, show_all -- ought to leave a realized toplevel alone. show_all maps the window, and on Win32 mapping calls ShowWindow, which dispatches messages synchronously through GDK's window procedure, so anything GDK does there runs before show_all returns. Every frame between libgdk and Workrave.exe is trust=scan, so the path through GTK cannot be read from the dump. The on_screen_changed handler that calls gtk_widget_set_visual looked like a candidate but is connected only under fullscreen_grab, which is false whenever Harpoon is available, as it is here.
So this does not fix the cause; it stops the process dying from it and records where it happened. GtkUtil::get_hwnd returns nullptr for an unrealized widget and logs the caller, and the nine call sites that took a handle unguarded now skip their work instead of faulting. set_always_on_top becomes a no-op on an unrealized window, which is the right meaning: there is no native window to raise yet.
BreakWindow.cc:896 and PreludeWindow.cc:235 already tested the handle for nullptr, one line after computing it -- the same shape as the lexical_cast guard in 380ccc5cc. BreakWindow.cc:733, three lines below the crash, had the identical unguarded pattern, so fixing only line 730 would have moved the crash rather than removed it.
Also handles a null main_window in ToolkitWindows, where it is a raw pointer defaulting to nullptr, and moves init_filter's check ahead of the add_filter call that dereferences the same window.
HWND is forward-declared in the header the way windows.h declares it rather than including windows.h, which this header would otherwise pull into most of the ui; verified that both declaration orders compile. Edge.cc keeps its raw use: it is inside on_realize, where the window exists by definition.
Builds on macOS, which does not compile any of the changed paths. The Windows build is unverified.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit bdbee2aab5f03b2447a06921ef06dd1859262056 Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-06T19:41:46+02:00
fix(core): say why a statistics file was rejected
load() treated an unreadable file, a wrong magic tag and an unsupported version identically: ok goes false, the parse loop never runs, and the caller quietly starts a fresh day. Only the first of those was reported, so a corrupted or downgraded historystats looked exactly like a first run and a user losing their history had nothing to go on.
Both remaining cases now log, naming the file and what was wrong with it. load takes the path for that reason; both callers already had it.
Behaviour is unchanged: a rejected file is still ignored rather than treated as fatal, which is right for statistics.
Verified against each case:
absent stream not good, load is a no-op as before empty does not look like a statistics file (tag '') wrong magic does not look like a statistics file (tag 'hello') version 9 unsupported statistics version 9 version 3, 4 accepted
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit 5e4f876d57e2bbd618fb900caacbc7e4963b0dc0 Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-06T19:28:51+02:00
fix(core): don't let a failed statistics write terminate the process
Crash group 2683968e is an uncaught C++ exception (0x20474343) with Core::set_powersave -> Statistics::update -> Statistics::save_day on the stack. save_day writes today's statistics to todaystats.tmp and then calls std::filesystem::rename, the overload that throws. Nothing catches it, so a rename that cannot complete -- the file locked by a backup or virus scanner, a state directory that has become unwritable -- terminates the process. update() runs on the periodic heartbeat, so once that condition holds the process dies on the next tick and keeps doing so.
Reproduced with the old code against a rename that cannot succeed:
old: THREW filesystem_error: in rename: Is a directory new: logged: failed to rename (Is a directory), returned normally
The error_code overloads are now used for rename, remove and is_regular_file, and every failure is logged with the path and the reason. Nothing on this path throws any more.
Two further problems in the same code:
- save_day(stats, ofstream&) closed the stream it was handed. It did not open it and has no business closing it, and day_to_history then closed the same stream a second time, which merely sets failbit on an already-closed file but hid whether the write had actually succeeded. The writer now only writes; each caller closes what it opened and checks the result.
- save_day renamed the temporary file over todaystats without ever checking that the write succeeded. A short write would have replaced good statistics with a truncated file. The rename now happens only once the stream closed cleanly, and the temporary file is removed otherwise.
The read paths log too, distinguishing a file that is absent, which is normal on a first run, from one that exists and cannot be read.
corenext carries the same code and gets the same fix, though it is not built for the Windows release these crashes come from.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit f530ccfdad08905915f2c851eec92f03b8242ba7 Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-06T17:51:38+02:00
feat(tools): record the Workrave release a symbol belongs to
The version stored with a symbol was the DLL's own FileVersion, so glib's symbols said 2.88.2.0. That describes the library, not which Workrave shipped it, which is what you want when deciding whether a symbol is still needed.
--version now sets it, and the release passes ${WORKRAVE_VERSION}. It falls back to the FileVersion for an ad-hoc run with no release to name. Where one library build shipped in several releases, name the first: the symbol is keyed on the code id, which does not change between them.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit b7ed4b73b55be8c8f36574cb27460b57b12dd790 Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-06T17:30:21+02:00
fix(tools): record the Workrave build that shipped the DLLs
Two different things are called a build id in a symbol upload, and this was sending the wrong one for the second. The MODULE line's third field becomes the symbol's build_id, the key the symbolizer matches; the upload's build_id form field becomes its build_tag, which records the build the symbols came from. Our own symbols show the intent: build_id 94A7D9F0..., build_tag 20260723-v1_11_1local.
The form field was being filled with the PE code id, which merely repeated the lookup key and discarded the provenance. It now comes from --build-id, which the release passes as ${WORKRAVE_BUILD_ID}, and falls back to the code id for an ad-hoc run that has no Workrave build to name.
The lookup key is unchanged and stays the code id, which is what the minidump reports for these DLLs.
Verified against the compose stack: uploading libglib-2.0-0.dll with --build-id 20260723-v1_11_1local stores build_id 6A3F7C5516C000 and build_tag 20260723-v1_11_1local.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit 003de65cabb21a63e3cd935afe71ecf8a6db4074 Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-06T15:50:42+02:00
fix(tools): use the basename of the pdb path from the CodeView record
A PE that does carry a CodeView record stores whatever path the linker embedded, which for our own binaries is an absolute build path. Using it verbatim as the symbol file name meant trying to write
portable_syms/C:/mystuff/tmp/builds/.../libsigstore.pdb.sym
and dying on the missing directory. The minidump reports only the basename, so key on that, matching what the crash server does when it builds the lookup path.
Found running the tool over the 1.11.1 portable bundle, where five of our own DLLs have real CodeView records; it now emits all 111.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit a87320166f6b8d41e2b96d27343e29ad41f83db9 Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-06T14:23:21+02:00
build(release): upload MinGW symbols as part of the Windows release
The GTK stack is bundled from MSYS2 without debug info, so nothing below our own frames symbolises in a crash report. upload-mingw-symbols.py recovers what it can from the export tables; this runs it at release time, next to the existing upload_symbols.
Symbols are taken from the staged install tree, ${SOURCES_DIR}/_output/Release/bin, where InstallDependencies.cmake puts the resolved runtime DLLs, rather than from /mingw64/bin. The two can differ: the symbols have to describe the binaries this release actually ships, because they are keyed on the code id, which is per build and not per version. MINGW_SYMBOLS_DIR overrides the path.
A failure only warns. By the time this runs the artifacts, the GitHub release and the appcast are already published, and the script runs under -e, so aborting here would fail a release that has in every other respect succeeded. It skips quietly when python3 or the staged tree is missing.
The token is fetched once from the signing service, where the existing symbol upload gets it per file.
Verified against a stub signing service and a live crash server, with a staged tree built from the MSYS2 glib2 package: six DLLs uploaded and recorded under their own code ids with the release channel and commit; a missing tree skips with a message; MINGW_SYMBOLS_DIR is honoured; an unreachable server warns and leaves the script running.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit 7bc94c93787d1f36ffcff3403c0c8544048f85ef Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-06T14:16:46+02:00
feat(tools): key MinGW symbol files on the code id
A nil debug id is shared by every build of a DLL, so symbols uploaded under it get applied to whichever build turns up. The crash server now looks a module with a nil debug id up by its code id first, so write that into the MODULE line instead. --id-source zero restores the old behaviour.
Verified against the compose stack: the six DLLs from the MSYS2 glib2 package upload and store under their own code ids.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit 52eb18b0102e9518ed817c1189109c06c90e15b6 Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-06T14:04:49+02:00
feat(tools): generate and upload Breakpad symbols for the MinGW DLLs
Crash reports from Windows are unreadable below our own frames. Workrave.exe is built with clang and gets real symbols, but the GTK stack we ship comes from MSYS2 stripped of DWARF and, more importantly, with no CodeView record at all: the DEBUG directory in those PEs is empty, so a minidump reports their debug id as 33 zeros and the crash server has nothing to look them up by. There is no -debug package in the MSYS2 repo to fall back on, and the COFF symbol table that survives holds only import thunks. The export table is the only symbol source left, and this turns it into a Breakpad .sym file.
Symbols are function-level and no better: an address resolves to the nearest preceding export, so anything static or inlined is reported under whatever exported symbol sits in front of it. A large +offset on a symbolised frame means the name is wrong, not that the function is big.
The all-zero debug id is shared by every build of a DLL, so one symbol file serves them all and the bundle has to be re-uploaded whenever it moves. Version strings do not disambiguate: the 2.88.2 glib in the repo today reports code_id 6A3F7AB6183000, while the 2.88.2 our users are running reports 6A3F7C5516C000. The PE timestamp and image size go up as the upload's build_id so the server at least records which build the symbols came from.
Verified against the real MSYS2 glib2 package and a live crash server:
1912 symbols from libglib-2.0-0.dll, 2063 from libgio-2.0-0.dll parsed by minidump_unwind::SymbolFile, the crash server's own reader 0x46b90 resolves to g_main_context_dispatch +0x20 six DLLs uploaded, six rows created once the import worker was running non-PE files and PEs without exports are skipped, not failed
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit fd545e38e4d84366284b3fbc3f27524d48400186 Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-06T02:05:29+02:00
feat(crash): log the pending exception before terminate aborts
Group 7f7cfd32 and its sibling 780a1b13 are 21 STATUS_FATAL_APP_EXIT reports from 13 installs, and none of them says what went wrong. STATUS_FATAL_APP_EXIT is abort(), and the unwinder loses the chain right at the abort boundary: past the ucrtbase frame every entry is trust=scan, Breakpad's brute-force stack scan, so the frames are guesses. One of those guesses resolved to the nearest preceding symbol and put a non-virtual thunk for Toolkit::attach_menu in the fingerprint, a function only ever called by the X11 tray icon, which does not exist on Windows. The dumps are unreadable.
What is missing is the exception message. glibmm calls std::terminate when a C++ exception escapes a signal handler into glib's C main loop, and the default handler discards what() before crashpad ever sees the process. This installs a terminate handler that recovers the pending exception with current_exception/rethrow_exception, logs its type and what(), and flushes, because the log is one of the report's attachments and has to reach disk before the process dies.
The dump still comes from abort, exactly as before: the handler chains to the previously installed handler and then aborts. Nothing in the logging path can prevent that, hence the outer catch(...) around it. It is installed only after StartHandler succeeds, so a terminate can never reach it without a running dumper.
Verified with a harness built from this code: an exception crossing a noexcept boundary logs "terminate called after throwing St13runtime_error: <message>" to the file sink and exits 134 (SIGABRT); terminate with no active exception logs "terminate called without an active exception" and also exits 134.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit a2535f8961142001d83aefd2301b13977f48d130 Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-06T01:35:22+02:00
fix: don't let unreadable exercises terminate the process at startup
ExerciseCollection::load guarded the main exercises file with !main_file.empty(), but AssetPath::complete_directory returns the bare name when nothing matched, never an empty string, so the guard never fired. A missing or unopenable exercises.xml therefore reached read_xml, which throws "cannot open file" exactly as it does for malformed XML. Nothing between there and main catches it, so the app aborted before it started.
That is what production is reporting: 22 crashes from 4 installs, while 34 other installs on the identical build read the same shipped file without trouble. The file is fine; on those machines it could not be opened.
The same call also parses every *.xml under the user's data directory, so a user's own broken exercise file killed startup the same way. Each file is now parsed inside a try/catch that logs the path and the reason and moves on.
Also fixes three related defects in the same function:
- exercises.clear() sat inside parse_exercises, after read_xml, so each parsed file discarded the previous file's exercises. A user-supplied file replaced the built-in set instead of adding to it. The clear now belongs to load(), and parse_exercises builds into a local list that is spliced in only once the whole file parsed, so a throw part-way leaves no half-built exercise behind. - The exercises search path and the data directories are the same directories on Windows and macOS, so the shipped file was parsed twice. Files are now collected before parsing and deduplicated. - Typo: execises_directory.
Left alone: on Unix the Exercises search path appends workrave/exercises to every data directory, including glib's user data directory that already ends in workrave, while this loop appends only exercises. The two disagree, but making them agree would move the user's exercise directory on Linux, so it needs its own change.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit 2ea2a094fe1efd02155784d48794583136ab2621 Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-06T00:51:42+02:00
fix: don't let an unparsable config value terminate the process
W32Configurator::get_value converts the registry string to the requested type with boost::lexical_cast and no handler, so a value that does not parse threw bad_lexical_cast out of the backend. Nothing above catches it: Configurator::get_value(key, int32_t&) has a bad_lexical_cast handler but the call that throws sits above its try block, and neither Application::main nor WinMain has a handler at all, so the exception reached the CRT and killed the process at startup.
This is the largest crash group in production: 31 reports, all of them Break::load_timer_config reading a timer limit during Core::init, and the affected users cannot start Workrave at all.
Every other backend already treats an unconvertible value as a failed read — IniConfigurator and XmlConfigurator wrap their conversions and return no value — so W32Configurator now does the same and logs the key and value it could not convert.
Also guards the backend call in Configurator::get_value, which set_value(..., CONFIG_FLAG_INITIAL) uses to test for an existing value, and adds logging to the five bad_lexical_cast handlers in the typed getters, which discarded the error silently.
The new test asserts the contract that a bad value never throws. It cannot reproduce the Windows path: W32Configurator is not built on other platforms, and the backends that are testable already handled this.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit de766edc1ce7cb03691cd623cfd4c2974322c53a Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-06T00:46:20+02:00
fix: initialize break config locals from their defaults
Configurator::get_value leaves its out parameter untouched and returns false when the key is missing or cannot be parsed, and every caller here ignores the return value. The locals were uninitialized, so a failed read configured the timer from whatever was on the stack.
Seed each one from the same default_config entry init_defaults() writes, so a failed read falls back to the documented default instead.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit cdddfe3da335bf0fdc81856f6d536dbd4ac1d7d6 Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-09-06T00:43:37+02:00
fix: seed break defaults before reading the timer configuration
Break::init() called init_timer() and init_break_control() before init_defaults(), so both read configuration keys that init_defaults() is responsible for creating. On a first run those keys do not exist yet: Configurator::get_value() returns false without writing to its out parameter, and both callers ignore the return value and pass an uninitialised local straight on:
int limit; config->get_value(CFG_KEY_TIMER_LIMIT % break_id, limit); timer->set_limit(limit);
so a fresh install configured its timers from whatever happened to be on the stack, rather than from the defaults a few lines further down.
Seeding first is safe: init_defaults() only needs `config` and the default_config entry, both established earlier in init(), and it writes with CONFIG_FLAG_INITIAL, which skips any key that already has a value — so an existing user's settings cannot be overwritten by the reorder.
This does not address the uninitialised locals themselves, which still matter when a key exists but cannot be parsed.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

item.title: Workrave 1.11.1-15
item.description:
Workrave 1.11.1 has been released. This release fixes several Windows installation issues. This release contains no functional changes to Workrave itself; all changes are limited to the Windows installer.
- Bug fixes: - Fixed missing Microsoft Visual C++ runtime dependency on Windows, which could cause Workrave to fail to start with a "VCRUNTIME140.dll was not found" error - Fixed an issue where the installer would repeatedly claim Workrave was still running and refuse to continue, even when it wasn't - Fixed the installed version number not being shown for Workrave in the Windows "Apps & Features" list - Fixed an issue where the installer did not uninstall Workrave 1.10 when upgrading, leaving both versions installed side by side

AppIndicatorMenu only updates the D-Bus menu root pointer when the operation mode changes, but not when the menu model itself updates (e.g., when dynamic menu items change due to timers, mode switches, etc.). This leaves the AppIndicator with a stale/invalid menu pointer.

commit 607903d0846e001378f2d229e314b6cb615aeef5 Author: Łukasz Wojniłowicz Date: 2025-04-24T18:07:36+02:00
Fix open_window on system tray reloads
Fixes #612
Short unavailabilities of the system tray cause the status window to appear. This can happen, when Sway reloads or shortly after waking a monitor from sleep. The window has to be closed, which is cumbersome.
This patch fixes this by introducing a short delay to showing the window, which gives the system tray time to reappear. It also checks, if there is any monitor to show the window on, before showing it, mainly for not setting the status window setting to enabled, which causes it to reappear after waking up a monitor.

document Autoconf Macro Archive as a requirement
The macro AX_CXX_COMPILE_STDCXX_11 is a part of Autoconf Macro Archive and was commited verbatim before. In order to keep git changelogs more sane, all m4/*.m4 files were deleted. Now you need this macro to come from Autoconf Macro Archive. The macro first appeared in version 2012.04.04 of the archive. Initially it had only one parameter. The second parameter which was specified as [mandatory] before this commit is the default and can be safely ommitted for compatibility.

commit 77e09d41ca180db3cea0b44f7eda895678010de1 Author: Mateusz Jończyk Date: 2014-02-15T22:03:40+01:00
Improved support for locking the screen
It now works on most desktop environments, prefers D-Bus instead of executing raw commands and the code is much better organized.
The code now supports two general methods of suspending: via DBus (implemented in ScreenLockDBus.??) and via CommandLine (implemented in ScreenLockCommandline.??). Both classes inherit from a single interface: IScreenLockMethod.
Windows screen locking support is integrated in a separate commit.
The code was tested on Unity, Gnome3, KDE, Xfce, LXDE and i3 as of Ubuntu 12.04.

- (BreakWindow::refresh) Remove WindowHints::set_always_on_top() from the W32 section. That call does not behave as desired if there are multiple break windows and force_focus is enabled. Instead add a call to W32Compat::ResetWindow() to ensure we hold topmost.

- New class W32CriticalSection
An RAII wrapper for Microsoft's CRITICAL_SECTION thread synchronization object that handles the initialization, locking/unlocking and deletion. The locking is thread re-entrant, unlike Microsoft's own critical_section class which is not.

commit 40a05cb9308cfb4ba0a4b7b3809cc5c26d846520 Author: Jay Satiro Date: 2012-09-16T08:41:24+02:00
New W32ForceFocus class to force window focus
build/cmake/frontend/CMakeLists.txt frontend/gtkmm/src/BreakWindow.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/BreakWindow.hh frontend/gtkmm/src/RestBreakWindow.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32Compat.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32Compat.hh frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32ForceFocus.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32ForceFocus.hh
- Abolish existing win32 force focus code in W32Compat
- New class W32ForceFocus
The new class contains several different hacks to force win32 window focus. Each hack is contained in its own function. 3 are implemented:
AltKeypress(): Simulate an ALT keypress to force focus AttachInput(): Attach to the foreground thread to force focus MinimizeRestore(): Minimize and restore a dummy window to force focus
AttachInput() is a rewrite of the force focus method that was in W32Compat, and the other two are new. Each of the functions can spin their trick in an attempt to make the passed in hwnd (eg a Workrave break window) the foreground window.
Although the focus functions are public it is not always safe to call them directly, as at least one of them -- AttachInput() -- could deadlock our GUI main thread. Instead call ForceWindowFocus(), which creates a sacrificial worker thread to call the focus functions.
- New preference: advanced/force_focus_functions
As described above we have several functions that can be used to force the focus. This preference determines which of those functions will be called by the thread started by ForceWindowFocus(). If the preference does not exist then all functions are tried. The preference consists of one or more names separated by a comma with no spaces. The order is not important (subject to change). The names match to the focus functions' enumerated names:
all_functions, no_functions, alt_keypress, attach_input, minimize_restore
When all_functions is encountered then all functions will always be tried. When no_functions is encountered then no functions will be tried aside from a vanilla SetForegroundWindow().
The REG_SZ preference is evaluated internally as a string. Example: [HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Workrave\advanced] "force_focus_functions"="minimize_restore,attach_input"
- New preference: advanced/force_focus_on_break_start
This is a lighter alternative to advanced/force_focus that shouldn't cause any disruption. On BreakWindow::BreakWindow() this preference is read and cached locally as bool force_focus_on_break_start, and on BreakWindow::start() we call W32ForceFocus::ForceWindowFocus() if we're forcing focus on start.
Background:
We have to make sure our break windows are set on top with every call to BreakWindow::refresh(), however if advanced/force_focus is enabled then each call to set our window on top results in focus being forced to that window. Depending on the method that could cause flickering, simulated input, or any number of other undesirables. While I've made changes to mitigate this in the codebase we can also now virtually eliminate it by only attempting to force the focus once, on break start.
The REG_SZ preference is evaluated internally as boolean. Example: [HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Workrave\advanced] "force_focus_on_break_start"="1"

commit 4530ebe74a90a88d84360273629a1d74dc39f39a Author: Jay Satiro Date: 2012-06-29T07:28:41+02:00
Change harpoonHelper project to use static CRT
common/win32/buildone.cmd common/win32/harpoonHelper/src/harpoonHelper.vcproj
- (buildone.cmd) Enable command processor extensions (ENABLEEXTENSIONS) and delayed environment variable expansion (ENABLEDELAYEDEXPANSION).
On my systems with VS2008 and VS2010 I cannot run buildone.cmd successfully without both of those options enabled. They are already enabled in buildall.cmd.
- (harpoonHelper.vcproj) Use the static release/debug CRT when building harpoonhelper.exe.
C++ code generation for the helper links to the release/debug CRT DLL respectively depending on the configuration. A result of this is the 64-bit CRT DLL must be redistributed with Workrave because the version required may not be on the user's computer already. That's a problem because the helper is not in a separate directory where the 64-bit CRT DLL can also be placed. The only CRT DLLs that should be placed in the directory with workrave.exe are 32-bit types; there should be no 64-bit types.
Other solutions would be move harpoonHelper.exe to a 64-bit directory (eg something like %ProgramFiles%\Workrave\lib\x64) and include the 64-bit CRT DLL it was linked to, or include Microsoft's redist installer for the 64-bit CRT DLL and have setup run it before install.
This is not currently a problem with the 64-bit applet or 64-bit harpoon, both of which already link to the static CRT.

commit 2588eae32cc8223c1567810a6bf6d7c8ad147777 Author: Jay Satiro Date: 2012-06-01T09:05:28+02:00
New Win32 post-install autorun changer
common/src/win32/ChangeAutorun.c
- Standalone program that Active Setup can use to change a user's autorun settings.
The installer can set an Active Setup key to run this program. This way when each user logs on their autorun settings can be added or updated or unmodified according to the settings chosen during install.
Currently the installer can only change the autorun settings for the user running the installer. Using the Active Setup method ChangeAutorun.exe can be run automatically and quietly by Windows during each user's first logon after Workrave install.
For example the installer could offer an option to start Workrave automatically for all users, or new users only.
Here is the output of ChangeAutorun /?
This is a configuration tool added by this project's installer. This program is invoked by Microsoft's undocumented Active Setup. If you do not understand what this program does don't use it.
ACTIVE_SETUP_GUID: {180B0AC5-6FDA-438B-9466-C9894322B6BA} AUTORUN_VALUE: Workrave PROJECT: Workrave HKCU_PROJECT_KEY: AppEvents\Schemes\Apps\Workrave TARGET: workrave.exe TARGET_OPTIONS:
Options: -a Add autorun always. -b Add autorun only if user has never before used your project. -d Remove the autorun entry. -r Remove the Active Setup entry. -u Update existing autorun entry. -v Be verbose. If multiple arguments this must be the first. -z Show each passed in argument for testing purposes.
The 'Add autorun' options are mutually exclusive. Using either implies option 'u', which updates an existing autorun entry, if any.
Option 'r' removes the HKCU Active Setup entry, if any, and not the HKLM Active Setup entry. What that means is Active Setup will be reset for the user, and will run the next time the user logs on.

commit d70db4366b9ef97d5446b23cb7bee913ce8cca79 Author: Jay Satiro Date: 2012-06-05T07:09:18+02:00
Fix sound theme defaults for new users
frontend/common/src/SoundPlayer.cc
- (SoundPlayer::activate_theme) Do not check that the filename is not empty before testing it. An empty filename will now fail validation the same as if the filename does not exist.
Prior to this change a new user would not receive the default settings of a sound profile. Here's what happened with the break prelude sound, for example:
A new user doesn't have the following keys: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\AppEvents\Schemes\Apps\Workrave-crash\WorkraveBreakPrelude\.current HKEY_CURRENT_USER\AppEvents\Schemes\Apps\Workrave-crash\WorkraveBreakPrelude\.default
So Workrave sets HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Workrave\sound\events\break_prelude as ""
Later activate_theme() is called by register_sound_events() and it tests if break_prelude exists, and because it does it will not attempt to set the filename. The filename, empty as "", will not fail validation if it's empty.
As far as I know this was only a problem on Windows.

commit 81d78dfd4db7704591a23bbbcbf5d9e8737c69df Author: Jay Satiro Date: 2012-04-03T09:29:07+02:00
Rewrite OperationMode override behavior
backend/include/ICore.hh backend/src/Core.cc backend/src/Core.hh frontend/gtkmm/src/Menus.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/PreferencesDialog.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/Session.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/StatusIcon.cc
This is a rewrite of the OperationMode override behavior.
Among the significant changes:
Proper handling of multiple overrides at the same time.
Any override operation mode is more important than any regular operation mode. For example OPERATION_MODE_NORMAL as an override will override a regular operation mode of OPERATION_MODE_SUSPENDED, and as a result the active operation mode (var operation_mode) will be normal.
The operation mode overrides are valued in order of importance: OPERATION_MODE_SUSPENDED, OPERATION_MODE_QUIET, OPERATION_MODE_NORMAL. For example OPERATION_MODE_SUSPENDED as an override is more important than OPERATION_MODE_QUIET as an override. If both overrides are in the queue then the active operation mode (var operation_mode) will be suspended.
Proper maintaining and restoring of the last regular operation mode. Also the user can set an operation mode while an override is in place. In any case the regular operation mode will be restored and set active once all overrides are lifted.
Any overridden operation mode is no longer reflected in the status icon or 'Mode' popup menu entries. That was the result of a design decision to not call core_event_operation_mode_changed() during an override. That function in turn would likely cause other signals that could cause unwanted reentrancy and potentially adversely affect current operations or the restoration of regular operation. This change may also eliminate user confusion.

- Redesign worker thread code to fix bug.
W32AppletWindow::set_enabled( bool enabled ) created a worker thread each time it was called and enabled was true. That was incorrect. Optimized testconf.py
Testconf.py now writes out a makefile, allowing multiple workrave configurations to be built in parallel.
To invoke, do something like:
make distclean ./testconf.py > testconf.mk && time make -f testconf.mk -j12 -k
Any failing builds will remain in their respective testconf/* directory Succeeded builds will be cleaned out

item.title: Workrave 1.11.0-4
item.description:
Workrave 1.11.0 has been released. This is the first stable release of the 1.11 series, the result of more than three years of alpha, beta, and release candidate development.
Changes since Workrave 1.10.54 - Highlights: - You can now change the operation mode for a limited amount of time (#98, #305) - Workrave can automatically change the operation mode based on Windows Focus Assist (#255, #226) - High DPI support on both Windows (#650, Charlie Lin) and Xorg - Several new sounds contributed by Phil Dibbs - The Windows version is now 64 bit, with a modern Windows 11 UI theme - Modern desktop integration on Linux: StatusNotifierItem tray icons and a redesigned GNOME Shell extension supporting GNOME Shell 50, Wayland (experimental), and high-DPI/fractional scaling - An auto-update feature for Windows - ARM64 Windows support, including keyboard/mouse locking - The Workrave networking functionality was removed - The legacy Windows DeskBand/taskbar applet was removed - New features and improvements: - Workrave now follows the XDG Base Directory specification (#192) - A dark UI theme on Windows now follows the OS dark/light mode setting (#214, #529) - The default sound theme was changed to the "Subtle" theme (#362) - It is no longer required to accept the GPL license on installation on Windows (#648) - The Windows installer now asks whether to install Workrave per-user or system-wide - The D-Bus utility (gdbus) is no longer installed by default by the installer - Added examples of usage with swaybar (#597, J. J. Ramsey) - Ported the Workrave Python scripts for waybar, Yambar, etc. to dasbus (#557-#563, #627, J. J. Ramsey) - Allow Workrave to ignore idle inhibitors if possible (#596, J. J. Ramsey) - A portable version is now available for Windows and Linux - Desktop integration: - Support for the StatusNotifierItem protocol (#447) - The redesigned GNOME Shell extension supports GNOME Shell 50 and fixes several extension issues beyond the support already available in Workrave 1.10 (#396, #582, #661) - Added DPI scaling support for the GNOME Shell extension on Xorg, and fixed Wayland detection - Use the GNOME Shell extension to display prelude windows (#621) - Added Cinnamon applet support with GTK 4 (#487) - Fixed Wayland activity monitoring on KDE, and improved layer-shell support on other Wayland compositors - Handle the screen lock shortcut during breaks under Xorg - Enable application autostart across all Linux desktop managers (#548, Jon Petrissans) - Notable bug fixes (spanning the full 1.11 development cycle): - Fixed crash when a monitor is powered off (#606) - Fixed an empty AppIndicator menu (#556, #614, wojnilowicz) - Fixed the tray icon not appearing on waybar, swaybar, or wf-shell (#555, #613, wojnilowicz) - Fixed the status window showing when Sway reloads despite being disabled (#612, #615, wojnilowicz) - Fixed the Rest Break window appearing in the top left corner in "No Lock" mode (#663, #664, ValdikSS) - Fixed a crash on wlroots compositors when a break starts (#550, #552, #553, #554, Kirill Primak) - Fixed high DPI fractional scaling on Windows - Fixed the application icon on Linux - Fixed DPI scaling with multiple monitors (#308, #315) - Prevented state and daily-statistics data loss by saving files atomically - Fixed focus changing unexpectedly after a break warning - Fixed the main window reopening after the screen was unlocked - Fixed the Rest Break window opening below other Workrave windows - Fixed exercises not always appearing on the primary monitor - Fixed issues that prevented sounds or the status window from being disabled (#443, #444) - Fixed Windows language selection, special characters in the tray menu, and unselectable menu items - Improved hibernate/suspend handling (#539, #540) - Translations: - Added Georgian translation (#669, NorwayFun) - Created and maintained the Tamil translation (#498, #579, #581, TamilNeram) - Simplified Chinese: complete overhaul (#385, #391, sr093906) and further updates (#645, Sisyphe42) - Updated Indonesian translation (#560, #653, Andika Triwidada) - Updated Italian translation (#359, #403, #489, #490, #496, albanobattistella) - Updated Polish translation (#423, #465, #484, ChuckMichael, Hanna Kraska) - Updated French translation (#545, WedoneOfficiel; fix #656) - Updated Brazilian Portuguese translation (#512, Paulo Haddad Martim) - Updated Dutch translation (#437, WKobes) and fixed several strings - Updated Hebrew translation (#361, Omer I.S.) - Updated Persian translation (#358, MSKF) - Updated Catalan translation (#338, Jordi Mallach) - Updated Spanish translation (#494, Cristian Martínez)

Update AppIndicator on any menu model update. Fixes #556
AppIndicatorMenu only updates the D-Bus menu root pointer when the operation mode changes, but not when the menu model itself updates (e.g., when dynamic menu items change due to timers, mode switches, etc.). This leaves the AppIndicator with a stale/invalid menu pointer.

commit 607903d0846e001378f2d229e314b6cb615aeef5 Author: Łukasz Wojniłowicz Date: 2025-04-24T18:07:36+02:00
Fix open_window on system tray reloads
Fixes #612
Short unavailabilities of the system tray cause the status window to appear. This can happen, when Sway reloads or shortly after waking a monitor from sleep. The window has to be closed, which is cumbersome.
This patch fixes this by introducing a short delay to showing the window, which gives the system tray time to reappear. It also checks, if there is any monitor to show the window on, before showing it, mainly for not setting the status window setting to enabled, which causes it to reappear after waking up a monitor.

document Autoconf Macro Archive as a requirement
The macro AX_CXX_COMPILE_STDCXX_11 is a part of Autoconf Macro Archive and was commited verbatim before. In order to keep git changelogs more sane, all m4/*.m4 files were deleted. Now you need this macro to come from Autoconf Macro Archive. The macro first appeared in version 2012.04.04 of the archive. Initially it had only one parameter. The second parameter which was specified as [mandatory] before this commit is the default and can be safely ommitted for compatibility.

commit 77e09d41ca180db3cea0b44f7eda895678010de1 Author: Mateusz Jończyk Date: 2014-02-15T22:03:40+01:00
Improved support for locking the screen
It now works on most desktop environments, prefers D-Bus instead of executing raw commands and the code is much better organized.
The code now supports two general methods of suspending: via DBus (implemented in ScreenLockDBus.??) and via CommandLine (implemented in ScreenLockCommandline.??). Both classes inherit from a single interface: IScreenLockMethod.
Windows screen locking support is integrated in a separate commit.
The code was tested on Unity, Gnome3, KDE, Xfce, LXDE and i3 as of Ubuntu 12.04.

commit 93b3aa749d0f951f52b9a80395cfc591b9924bd3 Author: Jay Satiro Date: 2012-10-07T08:36:29+02:00
Check for visible tooltip during w32 break refresh
frontend/gtkmm/src/GtkUtil.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/GtkUtil.hh frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32Compat.cc
- (GtkUtil::get_visible_tooltip_window) New function to get the application's visible tooltip window.

frontend/gtkmm/src/BreakWindow.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/BreakWindow.hh frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32Compat.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32Compat.hh
- (BreakWindow) Add W32Compat class as a friend of BreakWindow.
- (BreakWindow::refresh) Move the w32 specific code to W32Compat::RefreshBreakWindow().
- (W32Compat::RefreshBreakWindow) New function for our w32 code from BreakWindow::refresh().

commit dfb2711fc390879927ba7470c809e052c9b79e87 Author: Jay Satiro Date: 2012-09-29T08:46:41+02:00
Add w32 topmost call in BreakWindow::refresh()
frontend/gtkmm/src/BreakWindow.cc
- (BreakWindow::refresh) Add a call to SetWindowPos() with HWND_TOPMOST to ensure that our break window stays topmost even over other topmost windows.
Prior to this change the call to W32Compat::SetWindowOnTop() --which is similar to what is described above-- in BreakWindow::refresh() was eliminated for compatibility with W32 force focus behavior. Ref: e5df39fb31b10745697406ebe2dc7c4283a75d05
All of the behavior of W32Compat::SetWindowOnTop() is now in BreakWindow::refresh() and is modified to be force focus compatible.
commit 92c6ace10f8872c8399b18516884375f6b8533ea Author: Jay Satiro Date: 2012-09-29T08:09:00+02:00
Change W32ForceFocus::MinimizeRestore() method
frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32ForceFocus.cc
- (W32ForceFocus::MinimizeRestore) Change dummy window coordinates to off screen. Change ShowWindow() calls to SetWindowPlacement() calls.
Prior to these changes the dummy window could be visible to the user during the brief moment when it was minimized and restored. It was very apparent on XP if using its default window theme.
commit 66d011d9199d19a0d2383059e3790b13e167389a Author: Jay Satiro Date: 2012-09-29T06:06:40+02:00
Fix minor bug in W32Compat::IsOurDesktopVisible()
frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32Compat.cc
- (W32Compat::IsOurDesktopVisible) Fix incorrect buffer size comparisons of bytes needed to max characters.
Prior to this change the incorrect comparisons would cause the function to fail if the bytes needed for a buffer was more than half its size.
commit 1a62a97d27b59c31275fcddb96d4879482089be1 Author: Jay Satiro Date: 2012-09-27T08:12:11+02:00
Add W32 function GetForegroundWindowTryHarder()
frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32ForceFocus.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32ForceFocus.hh
- (W32ForceFocus::GetForegroundWindowTryHarder) New function to retry GetForegroundWindow() a number of times.
- (W32ForceFocus::AltKeypress) - (W32ForceFocus::AttachInput) - (W32ForceFocus::MinimizeRestore) Use GetForegroundWindowTryHarder() instead of GetForegroundWindow() for more accurate results.
Prior to this change the three force focus functions above would test for the current foreground window by calling GetForegroundWindow(). Occasionally that call would return NULL because the window manager was in the middle of a transition from one foreground window to another. To remedy that I've implemented GetForegroundWindowTryHarder().
commit 95b6fe42c5267da9b48a56519cd01eef3cc8f693 Author: Jay Satiro Date: 2012-09-25T07:08:00+02:00
Add W32 functions to check winstation status
frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32Compat.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32Compat.hh frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32ForceFocus.cc
- (W32Compat::_init) Refactor W32Compat initialization.
- (W32Compat::WinStationQueryInformationW) New function to query winstation information.
- (W32Compat::IsOurWinStationConnected) New function to check if our process' window station is connected.
- (W32Compat::IsOurWinStationLocked) New function to check if our process' window station is locked.
- (W32Compat::IsOurDesktopVisible) New function to check if our thread's desktop is viewable by the user. If the desktop is viewable then the window station associated with our process is connected, unlocked and our desktop receives the input.
- (W32ForceFocus::thread_Worker) Do not try to force the window focus if our desktop is not visible.
commit 17d99f6ac1e1b25ccd5b7087e6aa5d38ad896472 Author: Jay Satiro Date: 2012-09-24T06:28:56+02:00

- (BreakWindow::refresh) Remove WindowHints::set_always_on_top() from the W32 section. That call does not behave as desired if there are multiple break windows and force_focus is enabled. Instead add a call to W32Compat::ResetWindow() to ensure we hold topmost.

commit 40a05cb9308cfb4ba0a4b7b3809cc5c26d846520 Author: Jay Satiro Date: 2012-09-16T08:41:24+02:00
New W32ForceFocus class to force window focus
build/cmake/frontend/CMakeLists.txt frontend/gtkmm/src/BreakWindow.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/BreakWindow.hh frontend/gtkmm/src/RestBreakWindow.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32Compat.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32Compat.hh frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32ForceFocus.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/win32/W32ForceFocus.hh
- Abolish existing win32 force focus code in W32Compat
- New class W32ForceFocus
The new class contains several different hacks to force win32 window focus. Each hack is contained in its own function. 3 are implemented:
AltKeypress(): Simulate an ALT keypress to force focus AttachInput(): Attach to the foreground thread to force focus MinimizeRestore(): Minimize and restore a dummy window to force focus
AttachInput() is a rewrite of the force focus method that was in W32Compat, and the other two are new. Each of the functions can spin their trick in an attempt to make the passed in hwnd (eg a Workrave break window) the foreground window.
Although the focus functions are public it is not always safe to call them directly, as at least one of them -- AttachInput() -- could deadlock our GUI main thread. Instead call ForceWindowFocus(), which creates a sacrificial worker thread to call the focus functions.
- New preference: advanced/force_focus_functions
As described above we have several functions that can be used to force the focus. This preference determines which of those functions will be called by the thread started by ForceWindowFocus(). If the preference does not exist then all functions are tried. The preference consists of one or more names separated by a comma with no spaces. The order is not important (subject to change). The names match to the focus functions' enumerated names:
all_functions, no_functions, alt_keypress, attach_input, minimize_restore
When all_functions is encountered then all functions will always be tried. When no_functions is encountered then no functions will be tried aside from a vanilla SetForegroundWindow().
The REG_SZ preference is evaluated internally as a string. Example: [HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Workrave\advanced] "force_focus_functions"="minimize_restore,attach_input"
- New preference: advanced/force_focus_on_break_start
This is a lighter alternative to advanced/force_focus that shouldn't cause any disruption. On BreakWindow::BreakWindow() this preference is read and cached locally as bool force_focus_on_break_start, and on BreakWindow::start() we call W32ForceFocus::ForceWindowFocus() if we're forcing focus on start.
Background:
We have to make sure our break windows are set on top with every call to BreakWindow::refresh(), however if advanced/force_focus is enabled then each call to set our window on top results in focus being forced to that window. Depending on the method that could cause flickering, simulated input, or any number of other undesirables. While I've made changes to mitigate this in the codebase we can also now virtually eliminate it by only attempting to force the focus once, on break start.
The REG_SZ preference is evaluated internally as boolean. Example: [HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Workrave\advanced] "force_focus_on_break_start"="1"

- (buildone.cmd) Enable command processor extensions (ENABLEEXTENSIONS) and delayed environment variable expansion (ENABLEDELAYEDEXPANSION).
On my systems with VS2008 and VS2010 I cannot run buildone.cmd successfully without both of those options enabled. They are already enabled in buildall.cmd.
- (harpoonHelper.vcproj) Use the static release/debug CRT when building harpoonhelper.exe.
C++ code generation for the helper links to the release/debug CRT DLL respectively depending on the configuration. A result of this is the 64-bit CRT DLL must be redistributed with Workrave because the version required may not be on the user's computer already. That's a problem because the helper is not in a separate directory where the 64-bit CRT DLL can also be placed. The only CRT DLLs that should be placed in the directory with workrave.exe are 32-bit types; there should be no 64-bit types.
Other solutions would be move harpoonHelper.exe to a 64-bit directory (eg something like %ProgramFiles%\Workrave\lib\x64) and include the 64-bit CRT DLL it was linked to, or include Microsoft's redist installer for the 64-bit CRT DLL and have setup run it before install.
This is not currently a problem with the 64-bit applet or 64-bit harpoon, both of which already link to the static CRT.

commit 2588eae32cc8223c1567810a6bf6d7c8ad147777 Author: Jay Satiro Date: 2012-06-01T09:05:28+02:00
New Win32 post-install autorun changer
common/src/win32/ChangeAutorun.c
- Standalone program that Active Setup can use to change a user's autorun settings.
The installer can set an Active Setup key to run this program. This way when each user logs on their autorun settings can be added or updated or unmodified according to the settings chosen during install.
Currently the installer can only change the autorun settings for the user running the installer. Using the Active Setup method ChangeAutorun.exe can be run automatically and quietly by Windows during each user's first logon after Workrave install.
For example the installer could offer an option to start Workrave automatically for all users, or new users only.
Here is the output of ChangeAutorun /?
This is a configuration tool added by this project's installer. This program is invoked by Microsoft's undocumented Active Setup. If you do not understand what this program does don't use it.
ACTIVE_SETUP_GUID: {180B0AC5-6FDA-438B-9466-C9894322B6BA} AUTORUN_VALUE: Workrave PROJECT: Workrave HKCU_PROJECT_KEY: AppEvents\Schemes\Apps\Workrave TARGET: workrave.exe TARGET_OPTIONS:
Options: -a Add autorun always. -b Add autorun only if user has never before used your project. -d Remove the autorun entry. -r Remove the Active Setup entry. -u Update existing autorun entry. -v Be verbose. If multiple arguments this must be the first. -z Show each passed in argument for testing purposes.
The 'Add autorun' options are mutually exclusive. Using either implies option 'u', which updates an existing autorun entry, if any.
Option 'r' removes the HKCU Active Setup entry, if any, and not the HKLM Active Setup entry. What that means is Active Setup will be reset for the user, and will run the next time the user logs on.

Fix sound theme defaults for new users
frontend/common/src/SoundPlayer.cc
- (SoundPlayer::activate_theme) Do not check that the filename is not empty before testing it. An empty filename will now fail validation the same as if the filename does not exist.
Prior to this change a new user would not receive the default settings of a sound profile. Here's what happened with the break prelude sound, for example:
A new user doesn't have the following keys: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\AppEvents\Schemes\Apps\Workrave-crash\WorkraveBreakPrelude\.current HKEY_CURRENT_USER\AppEvents\Schemes\Apps\Workrave-crash\WorkraveBreakPrelude\.default
So Workrave sets HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Workrave\sound\events\break_prelude as ""
Later activate_theme() is called by register_sound_events() and it tests if break_prelude exists, and because it does it will not attempt to set the filename. The filename, empty as "", will not fail validation if it's empty.
As far as I know this was only a problem on Windows.

commit 81d78dfd4db7704591a23bbbcbf5d9e8737c69df Author: Jay Satiro Date: 2012-04-03T09:29:07+02:00
Rewrite OperationMode override behavior
backend/include/ICore.hh backend/src/Core.cc backend/src/Core.hh frontend/gtkmm/src/Menus.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/PreferencesDialog.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/Session.cc frontend/gtkmm/src/StatusIcon.cc
This is a rewrite of the OperationMode override behavior.
Among the significant changes:
Proper handling of multiple overrides at the same time.
Any override operation mode is more important than any regular operation mode. For example OPERATION_MODE_NORMAL as an override will override a regular operation mode of OPERATION_MODE_SUSPENDED, and as a result the active operation mode (var operation_mode) will be normal.
The operation mode overrides are valued in order of importance: OPERATION_MODE_SUSPENDED, OPERATION_MODE_QUIET, OPERATION_MODE_NORMAL. For example OPERATION_MODE_SUSPENDED as an override is more important than OPERATION_MODE_QUIET as an override. If both overrides are in the queue then the active operation mode (var operation_mode) will be suspended.
Proper maintaining and restoring of the last regular operation mode. Also the user can set an operation mode while an override is in place. In any case the regular operation mode will be restored and set active once all overrides are lifted.
Any overridden operation mode is no longer reflected in the status icon or 'Mode' popup menu entries. That was the result of a design decision to not call core_event_operation_mode_changed() during an override. That function in turn would likely cause other signals that could cause unwanted reentrancy and potentially adversely affect current operations or the restoration of regular operation. This change may also eliminate user confusion.

item.title: Workrave 1.11.1
item.description:
Workrave 1.11.1 has been released. This release fixes several Windows installation issues. This release contains no functional changes to Workrave itself; all changes are limited to the Windows installer.
- Bug fixes: - Fixed missing Microsoft Visual C++ runtime dependency on Windows, which could cause Workrave to fail to start with a "VCRUNTIME140.dll was not found" error - Fixed an issue where the installer would repeatedly claim Workrave was still running and refuse to continue, even when it wasn't - Fixed the installed version number not being shown for Workrave in the Windows "Apps & Features" list - Fixed an issue where the installer did not uninstall Workrave 1.10 when upgrading, leaving both versions installed side by side

item.title: Workrave 1.11.0-3
item.description:
Workrave 1.11.0 has been released. This is the first stable release of the 1.11 series, the result of more than three years of alpha, beta, and release candidate development.
Changes since Workrave 1.10.54 - Highlights: - You can now change the operation mode for a limited amount of time (#98, #305) - Workrave can automatically change the operation mode based on Windows Focus Assist (#255, #226) - High DPI support on both Windows (#650, Charlie Lin) and Xorg - Several new sounds contributed by Phil Dibbs - The Windows version is now 64 bit, with a modern Windows 11 UI theme - Modern desktop integration on Linux: StatusNotifierItem tray icons and a redesigned GNOME Shell extension supporting GNOME Shell 50, Wayland (experimental), and high-DPI/fractional scaling - An auto-update feature for Windows - ARM64 Windows support, including keyboard/mouse locking - The Workrave networking functionality was removed - The legacy Windows DeskBand/taskbar applet was removed - New features and improvements: - Workrave now follows the XDG Base Directory specification (#192) - A dark UI theme on Windows now follows the OS dark/light mode setting (#214, #529) - The default sound theme was changed to the "Subtle" theme (#362) - It is no longer required to accept the GPL license on installation on Windows (#648) - The Windows installer now asks whether to install Workrave per-user or system-wide - The D-Bus utility (gdbus) is no longer installed by default by the installer - Added examples of usage with swaybar (#597, J. J. Ramsey) - Ported the Workrave Python scripts for waybar, Yambar, etc. to dasbus (#557-#563, #627, J. J. Ramsey) - Allow Workrave to ignore idle inhibitors if possible (#596, J. J. Ramsey) - A portable version is now available for Windows and Linux - Desktop integration: - Support for the StatusNotifierItem protocol (#447) - The redesigned GNOME Shell extension supports GNOME Shell 50 and fixes several extension issues beyond the support already available in Workrave 1.10 (#396, #582, #661) - Added DPI scaling support for the GNOME Shell extension on Xorg, and fixed Wayland detection - Use the GNOME Shell extension to display prelude windows (#621) - Added Cinnamon applet support with GTK 4 (#487) - Fixed Wayland activity monitoring on KDE, and improved layer-shell support on other Wayland compositors - Handle the screen lock shortcut during breaks under Xorg - Enable application autostart across all Linux desktop managers (#548, Jon Petrissans) - Notable bug fixes (spanning the full 1.11 development cycle): - Fixed crash when a monitor is powered off (#606) - Fixed an empty AppIndicator menu (#556, #614, wojnilowicz) - Fixed the tray icon not appearing on waybar, swaybar, or wf-shell (#555, #613, wojnilowicz) - Fixed the status window showing when Sway reloads despite being disabled (#612, #615, wojnilowicz) - Fixed the Rest Break window appearing in the top left corner in "No Lock" mode (#663, #664, ValdikSS) - Fixed a crash on wlroots compositors when a break starts (#550, #552, #553, #554, Kirill Primak) - Fixed high DPI fractional scaling on Windows - Fixed the application icon on Linux - Fixed DPI scaling with multiple monitors (#308, #315) - Prevented state and daily-statistics data loss by saving files atomically - Fixed focus changing unexpectedly after a break warning - Fixed the main window reopening after the screen was unlocked - Fixed the Rest Break window opening below other Workrave windows - Fixed exercises not always appearing on the primary monitor - Fixed issues that prevented sounds or the status window from being disabled (#443, #444) - Fixed Windows language selection, special characters in the tray menu, and unselectable menu items - Improved hibernate/suspend handling (#539, #540) - Translations: - Added Georgian translation (#669, NorwayFun) - Created and maintained the Tamil translation (#498, #579, #581, TamilNeram) - Simplified Chinese: complete overhaul (#385, #391, sr093906) and further updates (#645, Sisyphe42) - Updated Indonesian translation (#560, #653, Andika Triwidada) - Updated Italian translation (#359, #403, #489, #490, #496, albanobattistella) - Updated Polish translation (#423, #465, #484, ChuckMichael, Hanna Kraska) - Updated French translation (#545, WedoneOfficiel; fix #656) - Updated Brazilian Portuguese translation (#512, Paulo Haddad Martim) - Updated Dutch translation (#437, WKobes) and fixed several strings - Updated Hebrew translation (#361, Omer I.S.) - Updated Persian translation (#358, MSKF) - Updated Catalan translation (#338, Jordi Mallach) - Updated Spanish translation (#494, Cristian Martínez)
commit 2c94f4c64187fedb6a9e73353a5949a12c6fc224 Author: Rob Caelers Date: 2026-07-22T10:53:09+02:00
fix: remove VCRUNTIME140.dll dependency (#703)

J. Ramsey) - Ported the Workrave Python scripts for waybar, Yambar, etc. to dasbus (#557-#563, #627, J. J. Ramsey) - Allow Workrave to ignore idle inhibitors if possible (#596, J. J. Ramsey) - A portable version is now available for Windows and Linux - Desktop integration: - Support for the StatusNotifierItem protocol (#447) - The redesigned GNOME Shell extension supports GNOME Shell 50 and fixes several extension issues beyond the support already available in Workrave 1.10 (#396, #582, #661) - Added DPI scaling support for the GNOME Shell extension on Xorg, and fixed Wayland detection - Use the GNOME Shell extension to display prelude windows (#621) - Added Cinnamon applet support with GTK 4 (#487) - Fixed Wayland activity monitoring on KDE, and improved layer-shell support on other Wayland compositors - Handle the screen lock shortcut during breaks under Xorg - Enable application autostart across all Linux desktop managers (#548, Jon Petrissans) - Notable bug fixes (spanning the full 1.11 development cycle): - Fixed crash when a monitor is powered off (#606) - Fixed an empty AppIndicator menu (#556, #614, wojnilowicz) - Fixed the tray icon not appearing on waybar, swaybar, or wf-shell (#555, #613, wojnilowicz) - Fixed the status window showing when Sway reloads despite being disabled (#612, #615, wojnilowicz) - Fixed the Rest Break window appearing in the top left corner in "No Lock" mode (#663, #664, ValdikSS) - Fixed a crash on wlroots compositors when a break starts (#550, #552, #553, #554, Kirill Primak) - Fixed high DPI fractional scaling on Windows - Fixed the application icon on Linux - Fixed DPI scaling with multiple monitors (#308, #315) - Prevented state and daily-statistics data loss by saving files atomically - Fixed focus changing unexpectedly after a break warning - Fixed the main window reopening after the screen was unlocked - Fixed the Rest Break window opening below other Workrave windows - Fixed exercises not always appearing on the primary monitor - Fixed issues that prevented sounds or the status window from being disabled (#443, #444) - Fixed Windows language selection, special characters in the tray menu, and unselectable menu items - Improved hibernate/suspend handling (#539, #540) - Translations: - Added Georgian translation (#669, NorwayFun) - Created and maintained the Tamil translation (#498, #579, #581, TamilNeram) - Simplified Chinese: complete overhaul (#385, #391, sr093906) and further updates (#645, Sisyphe42) - Updated Indonesian translation (#560, #653, Andika Triwidada) - Updated Italian translation (#359, #403, #489, #490, #496, albanobattistella) - Updated Polish translation (#423, #465, #484, ChuckMichael, Hanna Kraska) - Updated French translation (#545, WedoneOfficiel; fix #656) - Updated Brazilian Portuguese translation (#512, Paulo Haddad Martim) - Updated Dutch translation (#437, WKobes) and fixed several strings - Updated Hebrew translation (#361, Omer I.S.) - Updated Persian translation (#358, MSKF) - Updated Catalan translation (#338, Jordi Mallach) - Updated Spanish translation (#494, Cristian Mart�nez)

item.title: Workrave 1.11.0-rc.2
item.description:
Workrave 1.11.0-rc.2 has been released.
- Improvements: - Allow Workrave to ignore idle inhibitors if possible (#596, J. J. Ramsey) - Add examples of usage with swaybar (#597, J. J. Ramsey) - Support GNOME Shell 48 - Update DBus example (#611, Emmanuel Ferdman) - Support for user defined colors (#619) - Port workrave Python scripts for waybar, etc., to dasbus (#627, J. J. Ramsey) - Phil Dibbs contributed new sounds (bells_ensemble, shangri_la, synth_harp, tinkle_bell, tuned_udu, woodwind_ensemble) - Support GNOME Shell 49 (#636, Alessandro Astone) - Keyboard/mouse locking now works on ARM64 Windows - Handle screen lock shortcut during breaks under Xorg - Add high DPI support on Windows (#650, Charlie Lin) - Use Gnome Shell extension to display prelude windows (#621) - It is no longer required to accept the GPL license on installation on Windows (#648) - Bug fixes: - Fix crash when monitor is powered off (#606) - Fix an empty AppIndicator menu (#556, #614, wojnilowicz) - Fix issue where the tray icon did not appear on waybar, swaybar, or wf-shell trays (#555, #613, wojnilowicz) - Fix issue where the status window shows when Sway reloads despite being disabled (#612, #615, wojnilowicz) - Update AppIndicator menu when menu content changes (#556, #652,ValdikSS) - Updated Translations: - Update Chinese translation (#645, Sisyphe42) - Updated Indonesian translation (#653, Andika Triwidada) - Fix French translation (#656)
